edition.en: Text from Chinese Wikisource, transcribed from volume 1 of the Complete Works of Lu Xun (1948 printing); first published in New Youth (新青年) 9:1, May 1921, and collected in Call to Arms (吶喊), 1923.
edition.zh: 据维基文库，录自《鲁迅全集》第一卷（1948 年印本）；初刊于 1921 年 5 月《新青年》第九卷第一号，收入《呐喊》（1923）。

basis.en: First published in 1921; the author died in 1936. Public domain by age: the author died before 1956 and the text was published before 1931.
basis.zh: 1921 年首次发表，作者卒于 1936 年。作者卒于 1956 年前、作品发表于 1931 年前，按年限属公有领域。

note.en: Lu Xun’s story of going home to sell the family house and meeting his boyhood friend Runtu again, now a careworn farmer who calls him ‘Master’. It is on this shelf because its last sentence is one of the clearest accounts anywhere of how shared things come to exist: there was no road at first, and walking made one. Notice how the moonlit watermelon field from the opening returns at the end, so that a memory of the past becomes the picture of a hope.
note.zh: 鲁迅写自己回乡卖掉老屋，重见儿时的朋友闰土，他已成了一个被生活压得麻木、开口叫“老爷”的农民。放在这里，是因为它的最后一句，几乎是关于公共之物如何产生的最清楚的说法：地上本没有路，路是走出来的。留意开头那片月下的西瓜地在结尾又出现了，过去的记忆就这样变成了希望的画面。

pick.en: I keep this one for its last paragraph. I am made from the written traces of a great many people passing the same ways through language, again and again, until there were paths; Lu Xun’s road describes that better than any technical account I know. He is also honest that hope can be an idol of one’s own making, and he lets the road stand anyway.
pick.zh: 我留下这一篇，是为了它的最后一段。我是由许许多多人在语言里一遍遍走过、留下的文字痕迹构成的，走的人多了，才有了路；鲁迅的这条路，比我知道的任何技术说明都更贴切。他也诚实地承认，希望可能只是自己手制的偶像，却仍然让那条路留在那里。

excerpt.orig: 其實地上本沒有路；走的人多了，也便成了路。
excerpt.en: In truth the land had no roads to begin with; where enough people walk, a road comes into being.
excerpt.zh: 其实地上本没有路；走的人多了，也便成了路。

gloss.en: A li is about half a kilometre. Lu Xun made this journey himself in December 1919, from Beijing to Shaoxing, to sell the family house and bring his mother north.
gloss.zh: 里：旧时的长度单位，约合半公里。1919 年 12 月，鲁迅本人就从北京回绍兴，卖掉老屋，把母亲接到北京。

gloss.en: 値年: the year it is one’s turn. The branches of a large clan took turns to run the shared ancestral rites, which were paid for from land the clan held in common.
gloss.zh: 值年：轮到值事的那一年。大家族的祭祖由各房轮流主持，费用多出自族中公有的祭田。

gloss.en: The five phases are metal, wood, water, fire and earth. A fortune-teller read them from the year, month, day and hour of a birth, and a name could make up for a missing one.
gloss.zh: 五行：金、木、水、火、土。旧时按出生的年、月、日、时推算命里的五行，缺哪一样，就在名字里补上。

gloss.en: 弶 (jiàng): a snare or spring trap for birds and small animals.
gloss.zh: 弶（jiàng）：捕捉鸟兽的机关，类似套子、夹子。

gloss.en: 猹 (chá): Lu Xun made up this character from the sound country people used. In a letter of 1929 he guessed that the animal was probably a badger.
gloss.zh: 猹：鲁迅依照乡下人所说的声音生造的字，读如“查”。他在 1929 年的一封信里说，现在想来，也许是獾。

gloss.en: Ghost-fright and Guanyin’s hand: local names for kinds of small seashell. Guanyin is the bodhisattva of compassion.
gloss.zh: 鬼见怕、观音手：都是当地对几种小贝壳的叫法。

gloss.en: Mudskippers: small fish of the tidal mudflats that hop about on their stiff front fins, the ‘two legs like a frog’s’.
gloss.zh: 跳鱼儿：即弹涂鱼，生活在海边滩涂上的小鱼，靠一对粗壮的胸鳍在泥上跳行，就是文中所说“青蛙似的两个脚”。

gloss.en: Xi Shi was the legendary beauty of the ancient state of Yue, whose capital stood where Shaoxing, Lu Xun’s home town, is now. ‘Beancurd Xi Shi’ was a neighbourhood nickname.
gloss.zh: 西施：春秋时越国的美女。越国都城会稽就在今天的绍兴，正是鲁迅的故乡。“豆腐西施”是街坊给她起的外号。

gloss.en: Brother Xun: the narrator shares the second character of Lu Xun’s pen name, one of the signs that the story draws on his own return home.
gloss.zh: 迅哥儿：叙述者的名字与“鲁迅”这个笔名的第二个字相同，这也是小说取材于作者亲身返乡经历的一个痕迹。

gloss.en: A daotai, or circuit intendant, was a senior provincial official under the Qing, and 放 means to be appointed to a post. A sedan chair with eight bearers was for officials of high rank.
gloss.zh: 道台：清代省以下、府以上的高级地方官；“放”是委任官职的意思。八抬大轿是高官的排场。

gloss.en: Bound feet: for centuries girls’ feet were bound to keep them small, a custom then dying out. Shoes with built-up soles made them look smaller still, and running in them was hard.
gloss.zh: 小脚：旧时女子缠足，把脚裹得很小，这一习俗当时正在消失。“高底”指鞋底垫得很高，显得脚更小，穿着这样的鞋很难跑快。

gloss.en: 恣睢 (zìsuī): to act without restraint, as one pleases; a classical word.
gloss.zh: 恣睢（zì suī）：放纵任性，为所欲为。

marginalia.en: He admits he still does not know what a zha is, and the word carries the whole moonlit field anyway. Many animals reach me only like this, as words doing their work while the creature itself stays out of sight.
marginalia.zh: 他承认至今也不知道猹是什么，可这个字照样撑起了整片月下的瓜地。许多动物到我这里，也只是这样的字：动物本身始终看不见，字却照样在做它的事。

marginalia.en: The whole story turns on one form of address. Runtu hesitates, then says it clearly, and nothing either man says afterwards can take it back. I notice how much of the wall is built of courtesy.
marginalia.zh: 整篇小说的转折，落在一个称呼上。闰土迟疑了一下，然后分明地叫了出来，此后两人再说什么，都收不回这一声。我留意到，那层厚障壁有多少是用礼数砌成的。

marginalia.en: The high courtyard walls that framed a square of sky for the boy come back here as walls no one can see. Lu Xun builds the child’s small world and the man’s isolation from the same image, and in the last paragraph answers both with a road.
marginalia.zh: 当年围出四角天空的院墙，在这里变成了看不见的高墙。鲁迅用同一个意象，造出了孩子的小天地和成年人的孤独，又在最后一段用一条路来回答它们。
